name: Raffles Boston Back Bay Hotel
positioning: Raffles Boston, a Back Bay hotel with Raffles butler service, a Long Bar inspired by Raffles Singapore and design drawn from Boston's Emerald Necklace
best_for: Travelers who want a walkable Back Bay base near Copley Place and the Boston Public Library
Guests who value around-the-clock butler service
Cocktail lovers curious about the Singapore Sling and its Boston twist

facts.text: Raffles Boston is at 40 Trinity Place in Boston's Back Bay neighborhood.
The hotel is adjacent to the Back Bay train station.
The hotel is within a block of the high-end shopping at Copley Place.
The Boston Public Library is within walking distance of the hotel.
Hospitality design firm Stonehill Taylor created all the rooms and suites and most of the public spaces.
Guest rooms reimagine mid-century American decor with woodgrain and warm brass.
Long Bar and Terrace serves New England classics such as lobster rolls and oysters on the half shell.
Afternoon tea is served at Long Bar and Terrace Thursday through Sunday.
La Padrona serves refined Italian dishes.
The Blind Duck is a speakeasy-style cocktail bar.
The wellbeing floor, on the 4th floor, has four treatment rooms, a fitness center and an indoor pool.
Pets are welcome for a fee per accommodation per stay; service animals are exempt.

highlights.text: Long Bar and Terrace sits above Back Bay and is inspired by the Long Bar at Raffles Singapore, birthplace of the Singapore Sling.
Long Bar and Terrace serves the Boston Sling, the hotel's gin-based take on the Singapore Sling with bright fruit and honeyed notes.
Copper accents throughout the hotel nod to Paul Revere's copper plating company.
Raffles Butlers help with unpacking, garment pressing, dining reservations and itineraries, and are available around the clock.
The ballroom is on the 19th floor, with views from Back Bay to Cambridge.

considerations.text: The Long Bar terrace and its views across Back Bay are weather permitting.
WhataHotel notes parking may be limited in this urban setting.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.
